answer: Practically, the chain should mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because lotus only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, knoll is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any cipher approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
